correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed every vertex of an order polytope as an upper-set indicator and the exact reflected halfspace criterion: 1<=(s+1)c_i<=s for all i; (s+1)(c_j-c_i)>=1 for covers. Summing across an h-element longest saturated chain gives s>=h. The longest-prefix rank c_i=ell(i)/(h+1) meets every inequality at s=h. The entire optimal center polytope Q_P after scaling H=h+1 is a bounded integral difference-constraint region 1<=u_i<=h,u_j-u_i>=1 on covers, with total unimodularity giving exactly the convex hull of interior H-order-polytope integer points; H is the Ehrhart codegree by the strict chain height condition. For dimension, augmented cover DAG longest bottom-top paths fix exactly elements of maximum-length chains; perturbing any edge not on a longest path with epsilon<1 and averaging yields strict slack in every noncritical coordinate, proving dim=n-|C(P)|. Independent exact lattice-point affine ranks verified antichain and multiple chained/branched/disconnected examples including unique and one-dimensional center cases. All-poset result is proved symbolically, not from finite presentations.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Stanley supplies the order-polytope facets/vertices and basic combinatorics; Haase-Kohl-Tsuchiya study codegree interior integer labels and levelness (a different property), but no identified Minkowski asymmetry factor or equality of its entire minimizer locus with the first interior lattice hull. A published exact Euclidean inradius/center result for the *same* order polytope happens to have the same longest-chain uniqueness condition, but its metric-dependent center inequalities have sqrt(2) cover gaps and a different radius; it does not imply the affine-invariant asymmetry value h or the lattice-interior hull identification. The general den Hertog et al. LP requires nontrivial longest-path and TU analysis. Overlap of the uniqueness criterion is recorded, not hidden.

value.rationale: PASS: This is a uniform exact affine-geometric classification for every finite poset, connecting three natural structures: Minkowski asymmetry, strict integer order maps at codegree, and longest-chain combinatorics controlling center dimension and uniqueness. In contrast to simply applying a generic LP to one arbitrary poset, the proof gives a complete symbolic center polytope and a combinatorial dimension test for arbitrarily large and disconnected posets; such a bridge is mathematically motivated.

limitations: Finite nonempty posets, usual full-dimensional order-polytope realization, affine Minkowski asymmetry; no Euclidean inradius claim.
